newsitem.title: FRANCE: One-day strike hits France's Shell Berre complex.
newsitem.headline: One-day strike hits France's Shell Berre complex.

text.p: A 24-hour strike at Royal/Dutch Shell's Berre refinery in southern France slowed oil refining and halted deliveries out of the complex on Monday, a company official at the plant said.
Workers went on strike at the 128,000 barrels per day refinery near Marseille at 0300 GMT, he said.
Chemicals production was also hit, with some units such as the polymer-producing plant completely closed for the strike.
"Distillation and catalytic cracking are running at minimum levels. The refinery as a whole is at a slow pace and deliveries have been suspended," the official said.
A spokesman in Paris for France's largest union, the Socialist CFDT, said strike action was planned at the refinery for Monday and Tuesday over jobs and cost cuts.
Shell France was unavailable for official comment.
Unions have called a nationwide oil industry strike for Tuesday to protest about plans by several companies to reorganise the oversupplied refining sector.
Union officials said it was not yet clear which plants would join in, though union hoped to include major Total and British Petroleum plants near Marseille.
Management and union sources said a strike also disrupted the 80,000 bpd Reichstett refinery, run by Cie Rhenane de Raffinage in which Shell has a 65 percent stake, for about a day over the weekend.
Unions had planned a four-day strike at the eastern French plant, in which BP France, Elf Aquitaine and Mobil also have small stakes.
A nine-day strike at Elf's three French refineries ended on Friday after workers accepted concessions on pay and early retirement.
